title: Annotatio II NATIVITAS: Guitmund — PANI ET VINO COMMISCENTES; Impanent et Invinent heresy
pass_a_gloss: But you will also find on the contrary side, in the same eleventh century, those who called this sentence a heresy and tried to smother it in the very blade — namely Guitmund of Aversa, writing thus on the rise of the sentence just named, in book 3 On the truth of the Lord’s body and blood against Berengar: Now, he says, account must be had against those who, stormed by the Church’s reasons, can no longer deny that the substance of Christ’s body is in the Lord’s food; yet by no means believing that bread and wine are turned by the Savior’s words into His flesh and blood, but MIXING Christ WITH BREAD AND WINE, as by a subtler reason, they founded ANOTHER HERESY. … Wherefore … let them not bring other [causes], which is madness, that they should by their own authority, so to speak, IMPANATE AND INVINATE Christ. … But that Christ be IMPANATED and INVINATED no reason demands … nor did the Prophets foretell, nor Christ show, nor the Apostles preach, nor the world believe, except these very few HERETICS. … For they announce an IMPANATED AND INVINATED Christ … These His IMPANATORS the Lord Jesus Himself kills with His mouth when taking bread … He says, This is My Body; He does not say: IN THIS LIES My body; nor did He say: IN THIS wine is My blood.
pass_b_english: Same eleventh century, the other way: Guitmund of Aversa calls the sentence a heresy to smother in the blade.
Beaten from denying Christ’s body in the Lord’s food, some mix Christ with bread and wine and found another heresy — Impanate and Invinate by their own authority.
No prophet, Christ, apostle, or world taught Impanation; the Lord kills Impanators with This is My Body — not In this lies My body.
source_text: Sed & reperias vice versâ, eodem seculo undecimo, qui sententiam hanc hæresin appellarunt & in ipsa herba suffocare annisi sunt, GUITMUNDUM scil. Aversanum, de exortu modò dictae sententiae, ita scribentem, libro 3. de veritate corporis & sanguinis Domini contra Berengarium: Nunc, inquit, contra illos habenda est ratio qui Ecclesiae rationibus expugnati, jam quidem negare nequeunt substantiam corporis Christi cibo inesse Dominico; panem tamen & vinum per verba Salvatoris in carnem ejus & sanguinem verti nequaquam credentes, sed Christum PANI ET VINO COMMISCENTES, tanquam subtiliori ratione, HÆRESIN ALTERAM condiderunt. … Quapropter … nec alias ipsi afferant, quae insania est, ut Christum, ut ita dixerim, sua autoritate IMPANENT ET INVINENT. … At IMPANARI & INVINARI Christum, nulla … expetit ratio, nec Prophetae praedixerunt, nec Christus ostendit, nec Apostoli praedicaverunt, nec mundus, exceptis his paucissimis HÆRETICIS, credidit. … Christus enim isti IMPANATUM ET INVINATUM annunciant … Hos IMPANATORES suos ipse Dominus Jesus ore suo interficit cum accipiens panem … ait, Hoc est Corpus meum; non ait: IN HOC LATET corpus meum; nec dixit: IN HOC vino est sanguis meus.
